Pungent

PUN-junt · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Pungent is having a sharply strong smell or taste.

A pungent whiff of chlorine hit them the moment they walked through the pool's front doors.

Worked Example

The pungent aroma of fresh basil and garlic filled the kitchen the moment Dad started cooking.

The smell wasn't faint at all -- it was sharp and strong enough to fill the whole kitchen immediately, which is exactly what pungent describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

sharp: having a strong, intense smell or taste

biting: sharply harsh or intense to the senses

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

faint: barely perceptible

mild: not strong or intense in smell or taste

Where it sits · how intense the smell or taste — mellow → pungent → overpowering

mellow vs. pungent: A mellow smell is soft and smooth, nowhere near as intense as a pungent one.

overpowering vs. pungent: An overpowering smell is so intense it becomes hard to bear, even stronger than merely pungent.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — pung

Root — pung: to prick, to sting (from Latin pungere, 'to prick')

Suffix — -ent

Suffix — -ent: forms an adjective describing an ongoing quality (Latin -entem)

Put it together

Put it together: Pungent combines pung ('to prick or sting,' from Latin pungere) with -ent. The same root, by way of its past participle punctus, gives us the word puncture -- both describe a sharp, piercing sensation.

Use the root in a new word: puncture

Use the root in a new word: puncture: A tiny puncture in the bicycle tire let all the air hiss out within minutes.

Root Check

Word Choice

Pungent describes intensity, not necessarily unpleasantness -- pungent spices or cheese can be a compliment, unlike acrid, which almost always describes a harsh, unpleasant smell.
